subject.title: Feishu: duplicate final replies can occur after model failover from rate-limited primary

question: Should Feishu suppress or reuse an errored primary attempt's visible final when a fallback attempt later succeeds, and should that invariant live in the Feishu dispatcher or shared final-dispatch semantics?
rationale: Current code intentionally preserves some distinct later finals, while the issue asks to collapse the failover duplicate-visible-final case; choosing that boundary affects channel UX, shared reply delivery, and provider failover behavior.

options.title: Feishu-local closeout plus shared tests
options.body: Implement a narrow Feishu error/fallback closeout rule and add shared-dispatch regression coverage so failover duplicates are blocked without changing all channels at once.

options.title: Shared final-dispatch invariant
options.body: Move the invariant into `dispatchReplyFromConfig` so all channels get one terminal visible final per dispatch, accepting a broader compatibility review for intentionally distinct finals.

options.title: Sequence under durable fallback contract
options.body: Keep this issue open but defer code until #87561 decides the cross-channel final fallback and delivery-outcome contract.

recommendation.title: Feishu-local closeout plus shared tests
recommendation.body: Implement a narrow Feishu error/fallback closeout rule and add shared-dispatch regression coverage so failover duplicates are blocked without changing all channels at once.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main authorship touches both the Feishu reply dispatcher and shared final-dispatch loop involved in the boundary decision.
